neutral_facts.value: The prosecution alleged that the prosecutrix was abducted from her aunt's house and subjected to gang-rape by eight accused. The accused-appellant was one of the perpetrators. The prosecutrix initially described the accused as a short-statured man with a beard, but later changed her description. She failed to identify the location of the incident and provided inconsistent accounts of the number of people involved. The prosecution did not examine key witnesses, including the aunt, her husband, and neighbors. Medical evidence showed no significant injuries on the prosecutrix, and male semen was found on her undergarments but not analyzed. The accused-appellant was physically handicapped, which the prosecution did not address. The trial court convicted all eight accused, but the High Court acquitted two. The Supreme Court found the prosecutrix's evidence unreliable and the investigation flawed, leading to the acquittal of the accused-appellant.

quotes.text: Trial Court convicted all the eight accused under Section 366 and in addition to it, convicted accused 'KKM' and three other accused 'V', 'KT' and 'K', under Section 376(2)(g) of the IPC as well. On appeal, the High Court acquitted 'V' and 'KT'. The conviction of the other accused was maintained by the High Court. Thus out of the initial eight accused, six were held guilty under Section 366 IPC while 'KKM' and 'K' were held guilty under both Section 366 and Section 376(2)(g) IPC. The instant appeal was filed by only 'KKM'.

Allowing the appeal, the Court HELD:1.The prosecutrix P.W.9 had not mentioned the name of the Appellant in the FIR, instead she described him as Gitta (Short statured) with beard, even though she was aware of his name. No explanation has been offered by her in this regard.
